aboutSection.paragraph1: I am a product experience design leader with 20+ years of experience shaping OTT, enterprise, AI-driven, and multi-device digital products across global markets.
aboutSection.paragraph2: My work spans content discovery, personalization, design systems, team leadership, and scalable product experience strategy across TV, mobile, web, and operator ecosystems.

caseStudies.title: Interactive Video Platform Experience
caseStudies.tagline: Led global UX development for a video platform experience across TV, mobile, and web.
caseStudies.description: Led product experience direction for a global video platform that shifted from channel-first navigation to intent-driven discovery. The work aligned product goals, platform capabilities, and reusable UX patterns across TV, mobile, web, and operator ecosystems.
challenge: Linear, channel-first navigation no longer matched user expectations.
Users needed faster access to relevant content across large libraries.
Experience consistency was difficult across devices and markets.
Teams were delivering features without a shared product experience model.

approach.title: Experience Direction
approach.description: Defined product journeys across home, discovery, playback, profiles, and settings.

approach.title: Cross-Functional Alignment
approach.description: Connected product, engineering, and data teams around shared UX objectives.

approach.title: Reusable Patterns
approach.description: Established scalable UX patterns for discovery, playback, and personalization touchpoints.

approach.title: Design Governance
approach.description: Guided reviews and quality checkpoints for consistency across deployments.

outcomes: Created a scalable experience foundation for global video platform deployments.
Improved consistency across product areas and devices.
Enabled stronger discovery and personalization differentiation.
Helped teams move from feature delivery to product-led experience thinking.
caseStudies.leadership: The core shift was not only visual redesign. It was helping users make faster viewing decisions in a complex entertainment ecosystem.

caseStudies.title: Multi-Platform Entertainment Experiences
caseStudies.category: Cross-platform Strategy · TV UX · Platform Adaptation
caseStudies.tagline: Created connected experiences across iOS, Android, Apple TV, Smart TV, tablet, and web.
caseStudies.description: Designed a unified experience language across platforms while preserving device-native interaction behavior. The goal was consistency of product promise, not identical screen replication.
challenge: Users moved between mobile, TV, tablet, and web in a single journey.
Each platform had different input methods and content contexts.
Teams needed consistency without forcing identical UI behavior.
Engineering required clear adaptation rules across platforms.

approach.title: Platform Adaptation Model
approach.description: Defined how navigation, density, and interaction differed for TV, mobile, tablet, and web.

approach.title: Shared Design Language
approach.description: Kept recognizable patterns and hierarchy across all product surfaces.

approach.title: Journey Handoff
approach.description: Mapped cross-device continuity for discovery, playback, and account journeys.

approach.title: Implementation Guidance
approach.description: Aligned design and engineering through reusable patterns and interaction guidelines.

outcomes: Reduced fragmented platform experiences.
Improved consistency while enabling device-specific optimization.
Accelerated implementation with clearer design guidance.
Supported seamless user journeys across devices.
caseStudies.leadership: Great multi-platform design keeps the same product promise across different contexts instead of copying the same screen everywhere.

caseStudies.title: EPG & Content Discovery Innovation
caseStudies.category: Discovery UX · EPG · Search and Recommendations
caseStudies.tagline: Reimagined the electronic program guide for the streaming era.
caseStudies.description: Transformed EPG from a rigid schedule grid into a modern discovery experience combining live TV, on-demand browsing, search, voice, and personalized pathways.
challenge: Traditional EPGs were dense and difficult to scan at scale.
Users struggled to find relevant content quickly.
Linear grids did not reflect modern on-demand behavior.
Discovery needed to combine live, search, and recommendations clearly.

approach.title: Smart Menu View
approach.description: Simplified entry into personalized and editorial content areas for faster discovery.

approach.title: Enhanced Grid View
approach.description: Improved readability, hierarchy, and scanning cues for live schedule navigation.

approach.title: Search and Voice
approach.description: Supported quicker lookup and reduced reliance on manual typing in TV contexts.

approach.title: My Channels Personalization
approach.description: Enabled user-preferred content loops while retaining browsing control.

outcomes: Made content discovery more discoverable and intent-aligned.
Reduced browsing fatigue and decision friction.
Created scalable discovery patterns for global deployments.
Positioned EPG as a broader discovery experience, not only a schedule grid.
caseStudies.leadership: The redesign shifted EPG from static program browsing to a dynamic discovery model built around user intent.

caseStudies.title: AI-Powered Content Personalization
caseStudies.category: AI UX · Recommendation Design · Viewer Signals
caseStudies.tagline: Designed AI-assisted discovery that is relevant, understandable, and controllable.
caseStudies.description: Built personalization touchpoints across home, search, continue-watching, and detail journeys to reduce user effort and improve relevance without turning recommendations into a black box.
challenge: Generic discovery flows could not support diverse viewing behavior.
Large libraries increased decision fatigue.
Users needed transparency in why recommendations appeared.
Personalization required control, trust, and responsible guardrails.

approach.title: Behavior and Context Signals
approach.description: Applied watch patterns, session context, content metadata, and engagement signals.

approach.title: Explainability Cues
approach.description: Introduced clear labels such as because you watched and trending in market.

approach.title: User Control
approach.description: Enabled tuning, dismissing, saving, and preference control in recommendation loops.

approach.title: Responsible Experience
approach.description: Balanced relevance, editorial priorities, privacy, and repetitive-loop prevention.

outcomes: Improved discovery relevance across large content ecosystems.
Reduced search and browsing effort through better recommendation context.
Strengthened trust through understandable and controllable AI surfaces.
Positioned personalization as a strategic product differentiator.
caseStudies.leadership: Personalization succeeds only when users feel it is helpful, understandable, and still under their control.

caseStudies.title: Scalable Design System & UI Kit
caseStudies.tagline: Built reusable system foundations to improve consistency and delivery speed.
caseStudies.description: Established system layers across foundations, components, patterns, templates, and governance so teams could move faster with better consistency while preserving client flexibility.
challenge: Design decisions were being repeated across products and clients.
Implementation quality varied between teams and deployments.
Teams lacked a shared source of truth for UI behavior.
Customization needs often conflicted with consistency.

approach.title: System Foundations
approach.description: Defined tokens, typography, spacing, iconography, and accessibility interaction rules.

approach.title: Reusable Components
approach.description: Standardized navigation, content cards, controls, forms, and focus states.

approach.title: Pattern Library
approach.description: Documented recurring journeys for discovery, playback, search, profiles, and settings.

approach.title: Governance Model
approach.description: Introduced review checkpoints, adoption guidance, and implementation consistency checks.

outcomes: Improved consistency across product experiences and deployments.
Reduced duplicate design effort and repeated decision cycles.
Aligned engineering and design around one source of truth.
Supported scalable delivery across markets and product surfaces.
caseStudies.leadership: The design system became a delivery accelerator and quality framework, not just a UI library.

caseStudies.title: Product Evolution UI Framework
caseStudies.category: Framework Strategy · UX Governance · Team Capability
caseStudies.tagline: Created a scalable UX framework adopted across 30+ client platforms.
caseStudies.description: Built a reusable UX framework from scratch to standardize video product experiences across client deployments while enabling market and client adaptation.
challenge: No scalable UX foundation existed for repeated deployments.
Client customization increased fragmentation and rework.
Teams needed common patterns and stronger documentation.
Quality depended on one-off execution rather than reusable infrastructure.

approach.title: Framework Principles
approach.description: Defined scalable design principles for usable and consistent video product interfaces.

approach.title: Reusable Layers
approach.description: Created patterns, components, templates, and guidance for common product needs.

approach.title: Team Growth
approach.description: Built capability through mentoring, shared standards, and delivery quality rituals.

approach.title: Governance and Handoff
approach.description: Improved implementation quality through documentation and product-engineering checkpoints.

outcomes: Supported adoption across 30+ client platforms.
Reduced repeated design decisions and fragmentation.
Established long-term design maturity and governance foundations.
Transformed design from one-off execution into reusable product infrastructure.
caseStudies.leadership: This work built the long-term product foundation required for consistent global delivery at scale.
